title: Separate Squares II
summary: Given a 2D integer array of squares, each defined by its bottom-left corner coordinates and side length, determine the minimum y-coordinate of a horizontal line that equally divides the total area of squares above and below it, allowing for overlaps where areas are counted once.
statement: Given a 2D integer array of squares, each defined by its bottom-left corner coordinates and side length, determine the minimum y-coordinate of a horizontal line that equally divides the total area of squares above and below it, allowing for overlaps where areas are counted once.
constraints: Each square is [x,y,side] with positive integer side length.
The union area counts overlapping regions only once.
Return the smallest horizontal y-coordinate bisecting the union area; absolute error up to 0.00001 is accepted.
hints: Between consecutive horizontal square edges, the union width is constant.
Sweep y-events while a compressed segment tree maintains the covered x-length, then locate half the accumulated strip area.
Add the prior width times the y-gap before applying each event group; store strips, total them, and interpolate inside the crossing strip.
The strips partition the union by y, and the segment tree counts every covered x-coordinate once regardless of overlap depth.
editorial: The strips partition the union by y, and the segment tree counts every covered x-coordinate once regardless of overlap depth.

tests.explanation: The two disjoint unit squares balance at the beginning of the empty strip y=1.
A sweep tracks the union width of the overlapping squares rather than adding their widths twice.
